slides.title: Why Use Generics?
slides.content: Without generics you store items as object and cast back, losing type safety at compile time. A generic type or method works with any type T the caller chooses, and the compiler checks types for you.
slides.exampleOutput: (List<int> holds ints; ints[0] is already an int)

slides.title: Generic Methods
slides.content: A generic method declares its own type parameter in angle brackets after its name. The caller supplies the type, or the compiler infers it from the arguments.
slides.exampleOutput: (works for T = int, string, or any type)

exercise.prompt: A generic method's type parameter is:
options: Chosen by the caller at compile time
exercise.answer: Chosen by the caller at compile time

slides.title: Type Constraints
slides.content: A where clause restricts which types are allowed for a type parameter. where T : class means T must be a reference type; where T : struct means a value type; where T : new() means T must have a public parameterless constructor.
slides.exampleOutput: (only reference types can be passed as T)

exercise.prompt: The 'where' clause adds a _____ to a type parameter.

slides.title: Generic Classes
slides.content: A generic class has a type parameter that its members can use. Each instantiation fixes T to one specific type, giving you a distinct, type-safe class.
slides.exampleOutput: Box<int> and Box<string> are different, type-safe types

slides.title: The new() Constraint
slides.content: The new() constraint requires T to have a public parameterless constructor, so you can create instances of T inside the method with new T().
slides.exampleOutput: (compiles only for types with a public parameterless constructor)

exercise.prompt: The new() constraint requires T to:

slides.title: default(T)
slides.content: Inside generic code you often need an uninitialized value of T. default(T) returns null for reference types, 0 for numeric types, and a zero-initialized struct for value types.

exercise.prompt: Complete the method to return the default value of T.
hints: Use the default keyword with the type parameter T.
default(T) returns null for reference types and 0 for numerics.

slides.title: Generic Collections
slides.content: List<T>, Dictionary<TKey,TValue>, and HashSet<T> are all generic. The type parameters are checked at compile time, so you avoid casting and get IntelliSense for the stored type.

exercise.prompt: Complete the type so the list holds integers.
hints: The list should hold int values.

slides.title: Generics Review
slides.content: Generics let you write type-safe, reusable code: declare T on classes or methods, constrain it with where, use default(T) for uninitialized values, and rely on generic collections for strongly-typed storage.
slides.exampleOutput: (true if target is in the list)

exercise.prompt: Complete the method so it returns true when target is found.
hints: Loop over the list with foreach.
